Speaker: Greg Baran

This helps them organize their great ideas and structure their writing. In fact, learning how to get their ideas from their heads onto the page in an organized way is the single most important writing skill students need to learn. In this workshop, youâll learn a revolutionary writing method that uses colors to show students how to structure their writing. You can then use this easy-to-follow method the very next day to help your child become a confident and successful academic writer.

item.title: KEEPERS OF THE BOOKS: The Vital Importance of a Home Library
item.itunes:title: KEEPERS OF THE BOOKS: The Vital Importance of a Home Library
item.itunes:author: Jan Bloom
item.description:
Speaker: Jan Bloom
Throughout history, reading and owning books has been associated with culture, learning, and wisdom. In modern times, books have yielded to electronic information systems. Jan, a vintage bookseller, believes that the older books, written true to a Christian worldview and absent many modern biases, need to be rescued from destruction, read by the students of today, and kept safe for future generations. Jan gives guidelines on choosing which books to include in a home library, which books to borrow from a public library, and which books to send to the trash. Practical suggestions on book repair, deodorizing, and organizing will also be discussed.

item.title: Latin, Greek, Hebrew--Why your children should and how they can read them
item.itunes:title: Latin, Greek, Hebrew--Why your children should and how they can read them
item.itunes:author: Kevin Grasso
item.description:
Speaker: Kevin Grasso
When Harvard was founded in 1636, Latin was the primary language of instruction. The Yale valedictorians of classes 1785 and 1792 delivered their addresses in Hebrew. Even as late as 1857, a Greek salutatory oration was given at the University of Pennsylvania's commencement ceremony. Latin, Greek, and Hebrew had a central role in the education of Americans for the first 200+ years. These languages are now hardly studied and very few gain useful proficiency in them. I make a case for why learning these three ancient languages is so important for our culture. After showing their importance, I introduce modern learning science theories and how they can transform learning efficiency in any domain. I demonstrate how such theories can be applied to Latin, Greek, and Hebrew, so that your child (and you!) can learn these languages at any age and in the most efficient way possible (as a personal testimony, my son was reading Hebrew at 4). As a homeschool dad myself, I also discuss my firsthand experience of teaching my own kids Greek and Hebrew.

item.itunes:author: Joelle Hodge
item.description:
Speaker: Joelle Hodge
Track: Classical Track
From the True to the Good: The Role of Logic in Human Flourishing Classical education has long held that the pursuit of the Good Life requires more than moral aspiration--it requires trained judgment. In this session, we will explore how the study of logic in the middle-grade years (7th-10th) forms the habits of mind necessary for discerning truth, resisting error, and choosing what is genuinely good. Logic is often misunderstood as a merely technical or academic subject, but in the classical tradition it is a moral art, shaping students to love what is true so they may pursue lives ordered toward the good. Drawing from classical sources, contemporary reflections on flourishing, and practical experience teaching logic, this session will show how logic strengthens prudence, cultivates intellectual virtue, and supports a vision of human flourishing rooted in the True, the Good, and the Beautiful. Participants will leave with a renewed understanding of logic's formative power and practical ways to connect logic instruction to the moral aims of classical education.

item.itunes:author: Joones
item.description:
Speaker: Joones
It was not an oversight that the framers left education out of the US Constitution and the Bill of Rights. Education was never even mentioned in our founding documents. The omission of education clearly implies that the states have authority over education, and are not beholden to educational concepts, policies, and political philosophies of the federal government. The 10th Amendment clarifies that education should be regulated at the state level: The powers not delegated to the United States by the Constitution, nor prohibited by it to the States, are reserved to the States respectively, or to The People. It is up to We the People to take back control over education at a local level. Steve Jones from Convention of States will discuss the use of Article V to bring education solely into the control of the states and The People.

item.itunes:title: Learning to Read the Right Way - How to Teach Early Literacy Skills
item.itunes:author: Jeanna Young
item.description:
Speaker: Jeanna Young
Research emphasizes the importance of developing early reading foundational skills. Unfortunately, there are many children that fail to read proficiently due to lack of instruction in these early reading skills. They are often overlooked in hopes that children will "just get it" but can be detrimental later on. In this workshop I will show you exactly what early reading skills to introduce, how to introduce them, and at what age (starting at age 3). We'll discuss these essential skills and how mastery of them will lead to reading and spelling.
